en: The Sūtra on the Great Wheel Vajra Dhāraṇī Spoken by the Buddha.

Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying on Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa in the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus, as well as bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
With thirty-six thousand *sāhasra* as their leaders,
at that time, after the World-Honored One had entered parinirvāṇa and when the Buddha-dharma was about to perish.
Bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, and the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas,
surrounded him from all sides as he gathered to hear the Dharma.
At that time, a Vajrapāṇi deity questioned him regarding the essentials of the Dharma.
"After the Parinirvāṇa of the World-Honored One,
how should this Dharma-gate of dhāraṇī be upheld?
The Buddha addressed the Vajradhara deity:
Excellent, excellent!
You Vajras, for the sake of sentient beings in the final age,
have asked about this matter of benefit.
Reflect upon this well.
I shall, for your sake, analyze and explain matters of benefit and discourse upon the essentials of the Dharma.
The Buddha addressed the Vajrapāṇi deity:
Now, for those who wish to uphold the dharma-gate of dhāraṇī,
as well as to recite the sūtras, practice seated meditation, and cultivate various wholesome dharmas,
the foremost requirement is purity.
Second, to maintain a constant and resolute sincerity;
third, to apply oneself with diligence without regressing;
fourth, to repay the Buddha’s compassionate grace.
Fifth, one makes the great vow to diligently and precisely repay the kindness of one's teachers, monks, and parents day and night.
Sixth, one repays the kindness of the Bodhisattvas.
Seventh, one repays the kindness of the Vajras.
The eighth is to repay the kindness of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven;
the ninth is to repay the kindness of the Four Great Heavenly Kings;
and the tenth is to repay the kindness of the rishis who uphold mantras.
The Buddha addressed the Vajrapāṇi deity, saying:
"After my parinirvāṇa, during the period of the final dharma,
sentient beings will have meager merit, and the three calamities will arise in competition."
I have subdued the poisons of ghosts, spirits, devas, Māras,
and their like throughout Jambudvīpa, specifically within the land of Zhendan (China),
including all malevolent ghosts and spirits as well as the eighty-four thousand Māras.
Each of these Māras has five thousand retinues,
who have slaughtered immeasurable and innumerable sentient beings throughout Jambudvīpa in the south.
You Vajra-holders, having now heard this secret Dharma within this assembly, [should act accordingly].
O Vajras, listen to the method for upholding the dhāraṇī mantra:
first, quickly recite the Great Wheel Vajra Dhāraṇī Divine Mantra.
If you do not uphold this dharma-gate, [you shall fail].
Although all such spells may possess efficacy,
they still entail the transgression of practicing deceit and stealing the Dharma;
after one’s parinirvāṇa, one shall fall into hell to undergo the suffering of retribution, and thereafter fall into the realm of animals.
Such are the offenses incurred by practicing deceit.
If there be sons of good family or daughters of good family, as well as immeasurable celestial seers, vajrapāṇis, bodhisattvas, yakṣas, and all spirits and deities;
Listen well; I shall now explain for you the consecrated divine mantra (*abhiṣeka-mantra*).
By reciting it twenty-one times, one can accomplish all mantra-practices, and auspicious matters will swiftly attain fulfillment.
This mantra is that by which all Buddhas of the ten directions in the past attained Buddhahood through this dhāraṇī;
all bodhisattvas likewise reached the path of Buddhahood.
All vajras shall attain an indestructible body;
all rishis shall achieve accomplishment.
One who recites this mantra can perfect all mudrā rites and all maṇḍala rites.
When entering the Great Maṇḍala, one does not employ the ritual maṇḍala.
If one employs the ritual maṇḍala, various calamities will arise:

difficulties from heaven, difficulties from earth, difficulties from kings, difficulties from bandits, difficulties from water, difficulties from fire, all difficulties caused by yakṣas and rākṣasas, difficulties caused by devas, nāgas, ghosts, and spirits, all difficulties caused by māras, and all difficulties caused by humans.
Recite this mantra for seven days and seven nights while maintaining purity and burning incense.
Before the honored image, recite this mantra and repent for all transgressions of the three karmas; they shall all be extinguished.
All ghosts and spirits were filled with joy,
and every ailment upon their bodies was completely healed.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Vajrapāṇi spirit, the immeasurable celestial seers, and the bhikṣu Ānanda.
Listen well, you who uphold the Vajra-mantra;
for your sake, I shall establish a maṇḍala within the Vajra-deva realm.
You who uphold the Bodhisattva-mantra.
I shall establish a maṇḍala for you among the bodhisattva devas;
you shall uphold the celestial mantras. I shall establish a maṇḍala for you among the devas;
you shall uphold the nāga-celestial mantras.
I shall establish a ritual altar for you within the dragon palace;
you shall hold the mantras of the twenty-eight classes of spirits and deities.
I shall also establish a ritual altar for you among the spirits and gods of the heavens.
"You shall hold the mantra of the yakṣas and rākṣasas;
I shall establish a maṇḍala for you among the yakṣas, rākṣasas, and devas.
Thus spoke the Buddha to the Vajradhara deity.
When the mantra was being recited,
the mountains, rivers, and rocky cliffs all shook in six ways;
all the devas, ghosts, and spirits of Mount Sumeru were utterly unsettled.
All the dragon kings fled in great haste;
the clouds and rains of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven were all disturbed.
At that time, the World-Honored One then spoke this bodily incantation:

Namo satvārāya bhagavatāṃ tathāgatānāṃ hūṃ virāśe virāśe mahācakrara satva-satva śarati śarati taraye taraye vidamane saṃśamane trāmane siddhakalite svāhā. The Heart Mantra of the Great Wheel Vajra Dhāraṇī is as follows: Namo satvārāya (1) bhagavatāṃ (2) tathāgatānāṃ (3) hūṃ (4) virāśe virāśe (5) mahācakrara (6) satva-satva (7) śarati śarati (8) taraye taraye (9) vidamane (10) saṃśamane (11) trāmane (12) siddhakalite (13) svāhā (14). The Heart Mantra of the Great Wheel Vajra Dhāraṇī is thus spoken.

Namo siddhye cchivigāya tathāgatāya | Oṃ vilokaya vilokaya mahākāra varadavare sādhu sādhu śarati śarati taraye taraye vidhamani sampanne tāramati siddhākarṣi jyoti svāhā || This is the Heart Mantra. At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken this mantra, [said:]
He addressed the Vajrapāṇi deities, the mantra-holding ṛṣis,
the bhikṣus, the bhikṣuṇīs,
and others: "First, one must don new, clean robes, burn incense, and make offerings to the Vajra of Louti."
Recite the mantra for seven days and seven nights;
by burning only incense and using pure water while reciting the mantra one hundred thousand times,
all mantra-rites will be accomplished.
Henceforth, one may universally employ all mudrās;
indeed, if one wishes to maintain any mantra, it shall all be accomplished.
If one can constantly recite the mantra, [success will follow].
After the end of their lives, they will swiftly reach the stage of Buddhahood.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas such as Vajragarbha heard the Buddha’s exposition of the secret treasury of the Mahācakra-vajra-dhāraṇī.
We, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas Vajragarbha and the others,
each bring with us vajras as numerous as the sands of hundreds of thousands of Ganges Rivers;
each individual vajra has a retinue of one million times the sands of the Ganges.
Each [of these] led a hundred thousand Ganges-sands of treasure-guardians (*kośa-devatā*).
Each treasure-guardian, in turn, led the gods of the four heavens.
All descended, offering precious jewels and diamond mountains (*vajra-parvata*) to the Buddha, vowing: "May we, like the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajragarbha, all attain the stage of Buddhahood."
We, along with our retinues, shall joyfully receive and uphold this day and night.
Furthermore, we shall offer incense, powdered incense, ointment incense, banners, flowers, precious canopies, and food and drink of a hundred flavors to the World-Honored One,
making offerings to all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time— past, future, and present.
We, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas Vajragarbha and others,
shall likewise uphold this mantra for the sake of sentient beings in the final dharma age.
If there are good men or good women, or bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās, [who wish to recite it...]
One who upholds this Mahācakra-vajra-dhāraṇī should bathe before the image of the Honored One, don new and clean garments,
burn incense, and offer three trays of food and ritual implements while reciting it.
Since beginningless time, we have wandered through birth and death,
unaware of the number of kalpas that have passed,
and have slandered those of the śrāvaka vehicle, the pratyekabuddha vehicle, and those of the Buddha-vehicle.
They slander pratyekabuddhas and arhats;
they revile Mahāyāna bodhisattvas;
and they disparage those who practice the Dharma correctly.
They defile monasteries, temples, and stupas;
they defile the scriptures and practice the violation of the precepts;
their three karmic actions of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct are unwholesome.
Drawing blood from the Buddha’s body, killing an Arhat,
constantly practicing perversion by holding the correct to be false, committing the ten non-virtues,
being unfilial, and murdering one's father or harming one's mother.
I have committed all manner of various evils,
the number of which is unknown;
I now confess and repent before this honored image.
For seven days and seven nights, at the three times of day, recite this dhāraṇī divine mantra one hundred and eight times.
Use three ritual water-pitchers filled to the brim with pure water and insert willow branches into each.
Prepare three-tiered food offerings, as well as ghee, honey, curd, parched grain, tea, broth, honeyed lotus roots, and various kinds of fruit confections.
Before the honored image, dig a fire pit in the ground shaped like a blooming lotus flower.
Rub and wipe the four sides with red earth,
then recite the mantra over ten *jin* of charcoal;
the charcoal should be from the "King of Trees" wood, which is the *jǔnzǐ* tree.

Do not use other types of charcoal; instead, use three *dali* of *kunkuma* incense, two *dali* of *guggulu* incense, two *dali* of white sandalwood, and two *dali* of *agaru* (sandalwood) incense, along with half a *sheng* of clarified butter and half a *sheng* of honey.
Chop, hack, cut, and shear the five kinds of incense into pieces as large as a thumb;
place them in a single copper vessel and, using a copper spoon, mix them together while reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times.
Recite this mantra over the ghee, honey, incense, and other offerings one hundred and eight times.
The image faces east;
the practitioner faces west.
Kneel with lowered body and join the palms to form the *pūjā-mudrā*,
resembling the appearance of a blossoming lotus flower.
The two thumbs are placed side by side and pointed backward with a wrathful expression.
Join the two little fingers and extend them forward in a wrathful gesture;
the other six fingers are held as if cradling an alms bowl—this is called the *pūjā-mudrā*.
Disciple [Name], from [Place Name] District, [Place Name] County, [Place Name] Township, [Place Name] Village, here declaring my own name: [The remainder of the text follows]
If bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās state their original names as monks or nuns and the name of their original temple,
they shall announce this to all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
The path of karmic action of all the worthy sages and dark deities of the past:
Disciple [Name] and others,
on the eighth day of the [month] of the [year], at the fifth watch of the night.
First, in repentance, I open my heart and reveal my gaze,
entreating all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time:
all Buddhas of the past, all Buddhas of the present, and the Honored Buddha Maitreya of the future.
As well as the twelve divisions of the scriptures, the Sūtra Piṭaka;
all the great Bodhisattvas and the Sangha of worthy sages;
and all the Vajras and the thirty-three devas.
The Four Heavenly Kings, Śakra Devānām Indra, the Lord of the Underworld,
the Sun Deity, the Moon Deity, the Stellar Deities,
the Good and Evil Youthful Ones, and the benevolent deities who protect the precepts.
I bear witness that the disciple has confessed and repented;
may all their karmic obstructions be entirely extinguished.
Since beginningless time, the disciple...
Wandering through the six realms of saṃsāra and drifting in the cycle of birth and death,
they fail to recognize good and evil; before they have even encountered a Buddha,
they commit offenses, constantly engaging in theft and drinking.
Regarding the consumption of alcohol and meat, double-tongued speech, harsh words, and various forms of strife and discord;
regarding the countless instances of killing, the countless acts of sexual misconduct, and the countless instances of false speech—
today, at this very moment, I openly confess and repent.
Having performed this confession once, they shall not commit it again.
May the disciples, [Name] and others,
now fully declare their transgressions and calamities before the Buddhas of the ten directions.
Breaking the precepts by eating at night and constantly practicing deviant conduct,
they are born among the hungry ghosts, animals, barbarians, or the lowly and base within the six realms of existence,
always dwelling in places of unwholesome action.
At this very moment, I openly confess and repent.
Having confessed once, I shall not commit it again.
If there are sons or daughters of good family...
From the eighth day to the fifteenth day of the month,
one must offer fresh food every day; if one recites the mantra ten thousand times within those seven days,
a spiritual sign (*viṣaya*) will appear.
If one of superior capacity sees all the Buddhas and holy sages in a dream bestowing upon them the touch of their crowns and receiving their prediction,
then after receiving the Buddha-medicine,
they immediately realize the stage of the Bodhisattva Vajra-position.
They followed the Buddha as he departed.
If this is the sphere of those with middling faculties,
within seven days, following the previous procedure for making offerings, wind and rain will gather in thick clouds.
If one dreams of the Vajra-sages,
or sees sentient beings of inferior faculties,
one should perform offerings for seven days as prescribed previously.
No noble sages were seen;
for seven days there was neither wind nor rain,
and the banners and flowers did not stir.
This person, having committed the ten evil deeds and the five heinous crimes in previous lives,
lacked affinity with the Dharma; therefore, they redoubled their efforts in repentance,
performing it six times throughout the day and night.
We must immediately consume incense and perform recitation.

Homage to the Buddha! Homage to the Dharma! Homage to the Saṅgha! Homage to the twelve divisions of the scriptures! Homage to the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha! Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī! Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara! Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta! Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara! Homage to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Eleven-Faced Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Trātar, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva King of Sovereignty over Samādhi, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyarāja, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyasamudgata, and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya—homage to all these Bodhisattvas.
Each was surrounded before and behind by a retinue as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
and they addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
these are our bodhisattva retinues."
Each person shall take powdered incense, unguents, banners, flowers,
and jeweled canopies to make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions for the sake of sentient beings in the Dharma-ending age.
Those who practice and study the Mahācakra-dhāraṇī to augment their merit and virtue—
whether they be sons or daughters of good family,
bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, or brahmins.
The practice of the sūtras and the secret dharmaparyāyas of the sūtras shall be swiftly realized by mantra-holders and sentient beings of inferior faculties. We,
the assembly of bodhisattvas such as myself, also grant our seal of approval regarding cause and effect.
The Buddhas of the ten directions will touch their heads and bestow predictions of enlightenment upon those who recite this dhāraṇī.
Those who recite this mantra are reciting the fundamental dharma-gate of the immeasurable Buddhas of the past.
It can eliminate the root of all karmic obstacles of sin, causing them all to be extinguished.
If sentient beings of inferior capacity recite this divine mantra one hundred thousand times before a sacred image from the first day of the first month, [they shall attain the desired result].
Then, upon entering the maṇḍala, hang four banners of the Four Great Heavenly Kings.
In each of the four directions, place twelve banners of Vajrapāṇi.
Place eight banners of the Bodhisattvas. Directly facing the entrance, set out an image of Vairocana.
For the various offerings mentioned above, use a three-sided copper tray;
place various foods and drinks within the tray,
and use a copper vessel to hold non-glutinous rice, milk, and ghee-rice.
Prepare six *huān* of cooked rice on one plate, along with a copper spoon, Buddhist chopsticks, and various offerings of soup and side dishes.
Before the image, draw a square altar on the ground measuring four feet on each side.
Smear it with fragrant mud and write upon it with five colors;
each [section] shall be five cun, exactly according to the original prescriptions.
In the center, five new circular trays are arranged one above the other,
filled with scented water and adorned with willow branches;
to the south of the altar, the ground is excavated.
The fire pit is one foot five inches square;
within the one-foot area, it is shaped like a lotus flower,
and its interior is rubbed and polished with red clay.
Following the previous instructions for the five kinds of incense, ghee, honey, and so forth,
use a copper *śarāva* vessel to hold the ghee,
honey, and incense together in one place, mixing them thoroughly.
Use a new copper spoon to recite the mantra over this incense one hundred and eight times.
On the altar, place five lamps and a length of variegated silk measuring one chi and five cun.
On the first day of every month, for one day and one night,
recite the mantra one hundred and eight times,
making offerings as prescribed above.
For twenty-one days he changed his food once every seven days.
During this period of seven days,
no sensory objects appeared, nor was there wind, rain, or manifestations of ghosts and spirits.
If the Bodhisattva Vajra does not appear, it is because one’s karmic offenses are deep-rooted and grave.
Take the five aforementioned types of incense, blend them together, mix them with honey, and form them into pills.
Recite the mantra one thousand and eight times.
One should then take this incense, consuming twenty pills every morning on an empty stomach with water collected from a well at dawn (*jinghua shui*).
Each time one wishes to take the medicine, one must recite the mantra over the water twenty-one times.
Furthermore, one should recite the mantra over scented water to bathe the body and put on new, clean clothing.
Recite the mantra forty-nine times as an offering;
all internal obstacles will be completely eliminated.
These beings of inferior capacity have, from time immemorial, [been subject to these hindrances].
Using the property of the Triple Gem— the property of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha—
and constantly committing theft and adultery,
all the worthy and holy ones will incur immeasurable retribution for their sins.
On the [day] of the [month] of the [year],
the disciple [Name],
now before the honored image and before the holy monks of Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, openly confesses and repents.
All Buddhas, devas, nāgas, the eight classes of supernatural beings, and all spirits provide offerings and serve as attendants;
the great bodhisattvas constantly act as companions.
The mantra-holder shall eat but one meal per day.
By partaking of rice, milk, and curd from a fast-day meal, one gains physical strength and vigor;
one’s movements are unimpeded, one is honored by the multitude,
and all who hear one's words will believe and accept them.
All wealth and treasures will increase day and night.
One who practices this secret dharma-treasury of the dhāraṇī with constant faith and reverence should,
in a single pure, empty room, [perform the practice].
Recite the mantra with diligent effort day and night, and do not engage in miscellaneous worldly activities.
With single-minded devotion, uphold this practice until the end of this present life;
thereafter, you shall no longer undergo birth from a womb among the four modes of rebirth.
They always assemble together with the great bodhisattvas in one place.
Whether they be good sons or good daughters,
bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas or upāsikās, or brahmins, and so forth.
Those who uphold, recite, and explain it to others shall obtain immeasurable merit.
This sutra is a field of merit for sentient beings during the age of the Dharma’s decline;
it provides entry into immeasurable hundreds of thousands of dharani-dharmaparyāyas.
It is also the treasury of all sūtras.
If good sons and good daughters receive,
uphold, read, and recite it before a purified image, their soles will become calloused from lying prostrate.
He immediately beholds all the sūtra-piṭakas within the realm, as well as all the treasury deities, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattvas, preceptors, teachers, parents, and all honored images.
Having come from outside the assembly and seen these signs, this person [perceives them].
Keep your mouth shut and do not speak of this to others.
If you speak of it to others, both your precepts and your conduct will be ruined.
If there are good men or good women [who wish to hear it]...
Bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, brahmins,
and others shall read and recite the sūtras and the dharma-gates of secret dhāraṇīs;
they shall practice the three kinds of pure conduct, reciting the scriptures orally and refraining from speaking evil words.
With no malice in his heart and no defilement by the five desires of the body,
he must not dwell in the same place as the five kinds of Caṇḍāla women,
nor with the five thousand followers of the heretical hunters who carry countless [weapons].
One must not engage in conversation with prostitutes or widows.
One must not stay overnight at taverns.
Furthermore, one must not engage in frivolous debate regarding any of the scriptures with non-Buddhists, nor contend, quarrel, or slander the True Dharma or any gain and offerings.
If a son or daughter of good family makes offerings to a sacred image,
they must not eat that food themselves, as this would violate both their precepts and their conduct.
By giving it to poor children, they will obtain immeasurable merit.
Furthermore, one must not eat the leftovers of householders or renunciants,
nor may one eat at the homes of those who consume the five pungent roots, alcohol, or meat.
If good sons or good daughters were to eat such food, [they would incur transgression].
Those who have received and maintained [the teachings] but have broken both their recitation and their ethical conduct are no longer called "those who receive and maintain";

they lose both their spiritual power and their merit, and incur the offense of lying. When this Dharma was being taught, the bhikṣu Ānanda, bhikṣuṇīs, the gods of the Four Great Kings, nāgas, yakṣas, and the eight classes of beings, including gandharvas, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, upāsakas, upāsikās, five hundred brāhmaṇas, as well as the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, Brahmā Śakra, rākṣasas, humans, non-humans, and the Cakravartin kings were all present.
Upon hearing what the Buddha had spoken, they all rejoiced greatly;
they all realized the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti) and immediately attained the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
They all realized the stage of Buddhahood.

At that time, the World-Honored One expounded the method for painting images before an assembly of hundreds of thousands of millions of great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas from all directions and the three periods of time— past, future, and present.
A hundred thousand Vajragarbha Kings all came to the assembly;
a hundred thousand Yakṣa Heavenly Kings of the twenty-eight divisions all came to the assembly.
One hundred thousand celestial kings of fragrance all came together for the assembly;
one hundred thousand celestial yakṣa kings all came together for the assembly;
one hundred thousand celestial kings of lions all came together for the assembly.
A hundred thousand noble monks all gathered together;
a hundred thousand mantra-holding ṛṣis all gathered together;
a hundred thousand Śakra-devānām-indras all gathered together.
A hundred thousand wheel-turning sage-kings all came together in assembly;
a hundred thousand peacock-king deities all came together in assembly;
a hundred thousand nāga-king deities all came together in assembly.
A hundred thousand great Vāyu-deva kings all came together for the assembly;
a hundred thousand great Megha-deva kings all came together for the assembly;
a hundred thousand great Caturmahārāja kings all came together for the assembly.
One hundred thousand great rain-king deities all came together in assembly;
one hundred thousand golden-winged bird kings all came together in assembly;
one hundred thousand white elephant kings all came together in assembly.
A hundred thousand celestial kings of the sun all came together in assembly;
a hundred thousand celestial kings of the moon all came together in assembly;
a hundred thousand celestial kings of the lunar mansions all came together in assembly.
A hundred thousand asura kings all came together for the assembly;
a hundred thousand water-king deities all came together for the assembly;
a hundred thousand fire-king deities all came together for the assembly.
A hundred thousand kings of Yama gathered together;
a hundred thousand great terrestrial kings gathered together;
a hundred thousand mountain deities and celestial kings gathered together.
A hundred thousand river-deity celestial kings all came together in assembly;
a hundred thousand ocean-deity celestial kings all came together in assembly;
a hundred thousand benevolent deities of the five grains all came together in assembly.
One hundred thousand deities of dwellings all gathered together;
one hundred thousand deities who guard doorways all gathered together;
one hundred thousand deities of groves, gardens, flowers, and fruits all gathered together.
A hundred thousand *krīḍāhāra* benevolent deities all gathered together;
a hundred thousand sovereign deities of the seven treasures all gathered together;
and a hundred thousand celestial kings of the five kinds of pure wealth all gathered together.
One hundred thousand kings of sūtras all came together for the assembly;
one hundred thousand secret-treasury deva-kings all came together for the assembly;
one hundred thousand goddesses of merit all came together for the assembly.
One hundred thousand bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs gathered together;
one hundred thousand upāsakas and upāsikās gathered together;
and one hundred thousand gandharvas, garuḍas, and kiṃnaras gathered together.
A hundred thousand mahoragas and non-human beings gathered together;
a hundred thousand celestial kings of medicinal herbs gathered together;
and a hundred thousand celestial kings of exquisite garments for the four seasons gathered together.
A hundred thousand celestial kings, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, gathered together;
a hundred thousand great generals of the celestial seals, who protect and mind all sentient beings, gathered together;
and a hundred thousand wheel-turning sage-kings gathered together. At that time, when the World-Honored One was expounding this method of the painted image, [the assembly gathered].
The trichiliocosm shook in six ways.
At that time, mandārava flowers rained from the heavens;
fragrant winds arose from all quarters, banners and streamers moved of their own accord, and celestial drums resounded spontaneously.
The Buddhas of the ten directions and three periods of time emit the great light of compassion,
reaching down as far as the Avīci Hell;
when sentient beings of the six realms behold the color of this light, they...
They all recollected the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha, and realized unsurpassed bodhi.
Assembling in a great congregation, they wished to hear the method for painting the images of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
They took the silk and divided it into four layers.
Each [panel] shall be eight feet long and painted with silk treated with fragrant liquid;
glue must not be used for the painting.
The person who paints the image shall receive the eight precepts and eat pure food.
Having bathed and put on fresh, clean garments,
one should burn incense in a clean room, place a single bathing flask filled with scented water, and pour it toward the four directions;
this shall immediately establish the boundary of the sacred precinct.
First, draw a pond.
From the bottom of the pond, two branches extend downward.
Within the water of the pond, draw lotus flowers.
Among those that have blossomed, some remain unopened and hang downward.
Around the four sides of the pond,
sword-railings and stone pillars are installed.
All its pillars are adorned with various colors;
their tops are shaped like blooming lotuses,
within which vajra-jewels are set.
Upon each of its pillars, golden pearls were set;
in the center, a descending bridge was fashioned,
likewise adorned with variegated jewels.
On the thousand-jeweled staircase, one should depict a five-bay gatehouse;
above this, it is shaped like a multi-storied pavilion,
with seven gatehouses constructed ascending upward.
Above, it is adorned with *chīwei* (owl-tail) finials;
its tiles are all the color of green lapis lazuli,
extending down to the eaves.
From every single mouth, precious flowers are emitted,
with pearl bells suspended from their centers;
at the seven intervals between the stories, doors and windows are installed.
A large golden lock shall be installed at the center of the main gate;
all other gates as well shall be adorned with the seven treasures and colorful paintings.
At the center of the lower part of the main gate, an image of Vairocana shall be painted.
It is exactly like the Buddha’s image, including its proportions;
with Ānanda and Kāśyapa on his left and right,
as well as Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta is entirely adorned with the seven precious jewels;
on his left and right, two Vajrapāṇis are painted, made purely of golden color.
Holding a precious vajra in his hand, he assumes a majestic posture for subduing māras;
beneath his feet, a mountain of gold is depicted.
To its left and right, extending downward, two vajras are drawn, red and white in color.
Upon their vajra-summits are placed wheel-canopies;
their hands all grasp vajras,
adorned with colorful paintings.
Beneath his feet he treads upon Mount Vajra;
upright and majestic, as soon as he opens his mouth, his lips form a smile.
To the left and right of the Vajra, beneath his feet, there appear two lions.
Raising his head upward, he makes the gesture of a lion’s roar.
Before that image of Vairocana Buddha,
atop a large golden incense burner, rests a canopy made of the seven precious jewels.
Do not allow the incense smoke to be interrupted.
Before the incense burner, draw a blossoming lotus flower;
from the center of that flower, emanate a pedestal made of the seven precious jewels.
Upon the tray, seven golden tiers are painted;
within these tiers, gold, silver, lapis lazuli, coral, and pearls are placed.
Agallochum, frankincense, and ox-head sandalwood incense are set before the offering tray.
Paint four banners of the Four Heavenly Kings;
twelve small banners of Vajrapāṇi;
twelve banners of Bodhisattvas; and eight banners of Dragon Kings.
The practitioner prepares a single-layered mat upon the ground and draws the auspicious bird and grass upon the mat.
The practitioner kneels with palms joined in worship.
Whether it be a son of good family or a daughter of good family,
an upāsaka, an upāsikā, or a brāhmaṇa, and so forth.
Each person should draw their own tutelary deity,
with a joyful countenance and the form of a youth,
seated in the full lotus posture; thus concludes the method for drawing the image.
1. At that time, the World-Honored One taught the Dharma-body seal for performing all seal-methods. First, stand up and place the feet in the *tadita* (dagger) stance.
Directly raise both arms with palms joined;
separate the two middle fingers while joining the middle joints of the other eight fingers.
Bend both arms upward and place them upon the crown of the head;
this is the mudrā for protecting the body.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times. 2.
The Seal for Subjugating All Ghosts, Spirits, Heavenly Demons, and Māras. Second: Join the eight fingers together.
With the middle fingers of both hands, open the right over the left.
When this seal is formed, all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, Devas,
and others will be filled with joy.
3. The Seal for Eliminating All Obstacles of Sin and Karmic Hindrances. Third: Extend the two ring fingers, the two little fingers, the two index fingers, and the two middle fingers.
Place the left hand over the right and join the two elbows;
kneeling on the hams, recite the mantra one hundred and eight times,
or one thousand and eight times.
If there are sons or daughters of good family—
whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, or brahmins—
and all their various transgressions and obstructions of the past, future, and present.
All [obstacles] shall be completely extinguished without remainder.
When forming this mudrā,
one will always receive the protection of all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the eight classes of devas, nāgas, and others.
Having formed this mudrā,
the practitioner visualizes that their body, by means of this seal, becomes a vajra-body,
and thereby makes offerings to the three paths.
When performing the seal-making, one should bathe before the image of the Honored One,
put on fresh and clean garments, burn incense to perfume the hands,
and present various offerings of cakes and fruits of a hundred flavors.
The practitioner of the rite invokes all Buddhas of the ten directions and three periods of time— past, present, and future— as well as the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings,
the twelve divisions of the scriptures, and the Sūtra Piṭaka.
I announce this to the officials of the netherworld and the path of karma:
bear witness that for my disciples, [Name] and others,
all things pertaining to the past, future, and present.
All sinful karmas shall be completely extinguished.
That person shall attain the Vajra-samādhi within this Dharani-seal.
The Fourth Seal for Crushing All Maras, Devas, Ghosts, Spirits, Malevolent Exorcists, Fiends, and Evil Destinies: Stand upright with the feet positioned in the shape of a "T."
The left hand points downward in a wrathful stance,
visualizing weapons emerging from within it;
the right hand points upward.
Visualize that in his hand there is a pestle,
with which he subdues all māras and spirits, as well as all celestial māras;
he completely subdues every such person.
Manifesting a great wrathful majesty,
he bites his lower lip with his teeth,
his eyes glaring and his brows knitting in anger.
As for the mudrā of the pestle: clench the eight fingers into fists within the palms;
bend the joints of the thumbs and press them against the middle joints of the index fingers.
Within the heart, one should visualize a wheel of fire atop one’s own head.
Manifesting anger and resentment,
one should imagine that all celestial Māras, all evil ghosts, practitioners of sorcery, possessing spirits, beasts,
and their like die all at once.
Looking upward at the sky,
all the birds in the air, the flying celestial yakṣas,
and all other miscellaneous species died simultaneously.

5. The Seal for Subjugating All Celestial Demons and Spirits by Severing Their Heads: Standing with both feet in the shape of a "T" (the *dingzi* stance). This is the fifth seal for subjugating all celestial demons and spirits by severing their heads.
Grasping the right wrist with the left hand while keeping the front fist low is called the Vajra-Parśu Mudrā.
When performing this mudrā:
All devas, māras, ghosts, and spirits shall have their heads severed and die all at once. 6.
The Vajra-Blade Mudrā: For the sixth, the Vajra-Blade Mudrā, bend the ring finger and little finger of the right hand.
Pressing the two thumbnails with the thumbs in the palms,
extend the index and middle fingers;
raising the hands high is called the Vajrakartrī-mudrā (the Adamantine Sword Seal).
Visualize that this blade transforms into hundreds, thousands, and tens of millions of blades;
then all the ghosts, spirits, and malevolent demons will rise up simultaneously.
7. The Vajra Fire-Wheel Mudrā, the seventh: join the two thumbs together;
join the two middle fingers together;
as for the two index fingers...
Then, interlace the two ring fingers and insert them into the palms;
hook the left over the right.
Join the wrists of both hands and extend them upward with the palms facing downward.
The wrathful [deity] is like hundreds of thousands of flaming wheels.
The practitioner of the rite sits cross-legged before the Buddha,
with both elbows resting upon the knees.
One should visualize that the wheel of fire has twelve spokes.
Within each spoke, there are further hundreds of thousands of fire-soldiers;
each of these fire-soldiers transforms into hundreds of thousands more fire-soldiers.
Each [of them] commands immeasurable fire deities.
Should there be various devas, māras, spirits, or any kind of miscellaneous ghostly demons with retinues as numerous as the sands of the Ganges who harass and disturb sentient beings—
He is able to completely subdue all wheels of fire.
8. The Vajragarbha King’s Seal for Subduing Māras. Eighth: The Vajragarbha King’s Seal for Subduing Māras. He sits in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*).
Extend the index, middle, and ring fingers of both hands; within the palms,
the three fingers of the right hand point upward,
while the palm of the left hand is extended.
The hands press against each other; the right thumb presses the left little finger,
and the right little finger presses the left thumb.
It is named the Great Seal for Subduing the Heavenly Māras.
This seal has two names; one is as the previous seal.
The left hand points downward and the right hand points upward.
The interlacing of the fingers is performed as previously described;
this is called the Seal for Subduing All Māras.

At that time, the Tathāgata, together with all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings from the ten directions and the three periods of time—past, future, and present—numbering as many as the sands of hundreds of thousands of millions of Ganges Rivers, [proceeded].
When this seal was being proclaimed at the site of enlightenment,
there were further thirty-six kinds of māras: the māras of kings, the celestial māras, and the māras of space, along with twelve māra-kings,
who led eighty-four thousand demonic armies as their retinues.
Furthermore, there were five hundred celestial Māras, Pāpīyans,
each leading retinues as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, along with immeasurable armies of evil spirits and ghosts who devour the flesh and blood of sentient beings,
as well as all manner of malevolent enchantments and sorcery.
Furthermore, the Demon Master caused clouds to rise and rain to fall;
he brought down untimely frost and hail, destroying all the crops.
He then took his storage vessels and hid them away.
Throughout the world, they spread disease and kill sentient beings,
constantly making this their occupation and lacking any heart of compassion.
Furthermore, there are various classes of ghosts and spirits who suck the vital essence from people.
Immeasurable and boundless, with form or without form,
with hands or without hands, with feet or without feet;
they come without speaking, yet speak once they have arrived.
Together with the wrathful-eyed mind, they prostrate with all their implements.

Furthermore, there are the bird-headed celestial māras, the rat-headed celestial māras, the pig-headed celestial māras, the cock-headed celestial māras, the rabbit-headed celestial māras, and the ox-headed celestial māras.
All those celestial Māras and their like cast away all their weapons—
bows, crossbows, spears, shields, wheels, parasols, and all their armor—
and threw themselves before the Tathāgata, begging for their lives and speaking thus:
We, the hosts of Māras, take refuge.
Tathāgata, do not harm us;
we shall constantly provide protection for all the Buddha-dharmas.
If there are those who uphold and recite the sūtras,
they shall be free from all calamities,
and their wholesome dharmas will increase day and night.
All calamities were completely extinguished without remainder.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the māras, saying:
"You have all been able to resolve to attain bodhicitta."
They shall immediately attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
If any son or daughter of good family,
after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, receives and upholds this dhāraṇī, [they shall likewise attain it].
This person shall immediately realize the rank of the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha;
they will constantly receive the empowerment and protection of all Buddhas,
and all Bodhisattvas will always be their companions.
If sons of good family lack provisions,
may they always have them in abundance;
those who recite this mantra shall have bodies like nectar.
Its power and radiance are blazing and intense.
Should there be any bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, brāhmaṇas, or others who have violated the precepts,
it shall cause all their transgressions to be completely extinguished.
If good sons or good daughters recite this dhāraṇī,
they will increase in diligence and contemplation day and night.
May all sentient beings be freed from the suffering of shackles and fetters,
and may this merit be dedicated to the officials of the underworld,
to the paths of karma, to all ghosts and spirits, and to the Avīci Great Hell.
May all sentient beings undergoing retribution for their sins be completely liberated.

If there are sentient beings who, having committed all manner of evil karma in previous lives, now obtain a human body but suffer from various diseases, sorcery, malevolent spirits, demonic possession, epilepsy, or madness; [may they all be freed].
As for all calamities, regrets, the cries of birds, cold and heat,
and malignant diseases that do not subside for years or months—
if one recites this dhāraṇī one thousand and eight times, [they shall be cured].
All calamities and illnesses shall be entirely eliminated and cured.
If there are sentient beings of meager merit who suffer from short lifespans,
by reciting this dhāraṇī sūtra forty-nine times, they shall immediately attain an increase in their life span.
If there are those who encounter difficulties in childbirth,
they should recite this dhāraṇī sūtra forty-nine times;
the calamities will be extinguished and restored to their former state.
If one suffers from malaria that recurs every day, every two days, three days, four days, five days, or even seven days, or for half a month,
or for a month, or even for a year, and cannot be cured;
Draw well-water and place it in a *kamaṇḍalu*.
Before the honored image, consecrate the water one thousand and eight times with mantras.
Give three or two *liang* of this to the afflicted person to drink.
Take five pills of the aforementioned incense and consume them;
one will immediately be cured.
If it is a case of quotidian malaria, recite the mantra over a knife one hundred and eight times.
Draw a square or circle four feet on each side on the ground.
When the afflicted person has bathed and put on new, clean clothes, have them sit within it and administer incense; then recite the mantra one thousand and eight times.
They will immediately recover. If, however,
they have not recovered after many years and have become emaciated,
one should lie down with them and recite the mantra.
Draw a mandala on the ground before the honored image,
announce to the Buddhas, and pray that they will now save you from suffering.
Burn incense with a sincere heart and prepare food and drink of a hundred flavors.
By making offerings and performing acts of veneration, one will immediately be cured.
As for all manner of malevolent spirits, *jingmei*, *wangliang*, and transgressive ghosts who employ sorcery to consume the hearts of sentient beings,
or those whose upper and lower orifices bleed without ceasing— [these too shall be healed].
After some months or years have passed,
one should, before the honored image,
prepare a mixture of incense, clarified butter, honey, milk, curd, grain, rice, flowers, and sesame seeds, according to the previous instructions.
If one burns [the substance] in fire while reciting the mantra for seven days and seven nights—
performing the offerings as prescribed before and taking the fragrant pills with well-water from a deep well— one will immediately be cured.
This applies even to those suffering from the malady of epilepsy.
Following the previous instructions, offer various kinds of incense, food, drink, fruits, and cakes for one or two weeks; then you will immediately recover.
However, if it is a disease caused by celestial spirits that has persisted for many months without improvement, [further rites must be performed].
If one bathes with water consecrated by mantras and drinks four or five *he* (approx. 150–225 ml), one will immediately be cured.
If a person suffers from any kind of ulcer, scabies, or the five types of *kāmala* diseases, [the same shall apply].
Bathe with consecrated water for forty-nine days,
consume incense for twenty-one times,
and simultaneously recite this sutra before a sacred image.
If one recites this forty-nine times, the ailment will be immediately cured.
As for scabies or ringworm— regardless of whether they are dry or moist—
one should grind one *liang* of realgar and mix it with clarified butter (*sarpis*).
Recite this mantra one thousand and eight times before the honored image,
and thereafter bestow alms upon all sentient beings.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this dhāraṇī sūtra.
It was entrusted to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajragarbha and others, as well as to the bhikṣu Ānanda and the eight classes of beings, including devas and nāgas.
Surrounded by them from before and behind, they paid homage with reverence, accepted it with faith, and practiced accordingly.

The mantra for empowering white powder: Oṃ kanyaye śveta dhāya svāhā. The mantra for empowering red powder: Oṃ kanyaye āroḍha dhāya svāhā. The mantra for empowering yellow powder: Oṃ kanyaye pidhāya svāhā. The mantra for empowering blue powder: Oṃ akanye kṛdhāye svāhā. The mantra for empowering black powder: Oṃ akanye kuṇḍisena dhāya svāhā. I take refuge in the merits of all the scriptural collections seen through this dhāraṇī.
Furthermore, upon seeing any place of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa),
one should recite this mantra seven times;
its merit is inconceivable.
*Namo buddhāya kulani | namo dharmāya dhyāni | namo saṃghāya maitre | dharṣa vi | satvānām | Namo mahācakramudrā.* Cross the left and right hands, inserting them into the palms.
Place both thumbs inside the palms as well.
Holding the middle seal above the crown of the head,
place the left foot upon the right foot.
Recite the mantra twenty-one times.
Then, release it downward and let it disperse.
I prostrate to the Great Flower-toothed One with the Topknot, the Mysterious Trace Vajrapāṇi, the Great Wheel-King.
Ucchuṣma, Acala, Agnīmukha, the boundary-binding Mañjuśrī, or Krodha—
whether invoked as the Wrathful One who in an instant moves mountains and turns the seas,
subduing the hosts of rākṣasas and their poisonous minds— all are struck with terror upon hearing the recitation of the mantra.
Crushing and extinguishing the ten evils, you transform all sentient beings;
Transcending into the ocean of the Tathāgata’s merit and virtue, To protect the disciples who maintain this recitation, You resolve to praise and entreat them, responding with vows at their call.
O Great Vajra Pure Assembly, May the vajra mallet follow your will!
At this site of enlightenment, one pays homage to the applications of mindfulness; surrounding them on all sides, one establishes the boundary.
This is from the *Asamavajracakra-dhāraṇī-sūtra*. VA RA YA NA SVĀHĀ.
